## Bar / column, side by side

```{r g24-bars-setup, include = FALSE}
## The black rule at zero: as heavy as the baseline.
g24b_zero_lw <- 0.1 * g24_size / ggplot2::.pt
g24b_zero <- function() geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ$print$text, linewidth = g24b_zero_lw)
## Horizontal bars: the value axis along the top, vertical gridlines, no ticks and no rule on the category axis.
g24b_bars_theme <- function(media = "print") {
  list(
    g24_theme(media, horizontal = FALSE),
    theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y.right = element_blank())
  )
}
## Columns: the value axis on the right, and the left-hand copy the 2024 theme sets blanked.
g24b_cols_theme <- function(media = "print") {
  list(g24_theme(media), theme(axis.text.y = element_blank()))
}
## Labels of the light segments are black, of the dark ones white.
g24b_ink <- function(fill) ifelse(fill %in% c(p24[["red"]], p24[["blue"]], p24[["dark gray"]]), "white", econ$print$text)
```

Bars and columns are a small share of the 2024 print survey: 9 single-series column charts, 5 horizontal-bar charts, 2 small multiples of horizontal bars and 9 stacked charts, against 31 line charts.
A plain series is the brighter single-series red: all 9 single-series column charts and all 4 single-series bar charts in print, and 6 of the 7 single-series bar charts on the web.
Horizontal bars, stacked or not, put the value axis along the top, with vertical gridlines and no ticks, and start from a black rule at zero: all 10 of the 11 print examples that have a value axis, such as `20241005_EPC263` and `20250524_STC394`.
Columns keep the value axis on the right with each label above its gridline, and stand on a black baseline with ticks hanging below it under the labelled categories only: `20240504_USC067`, `20240803_EUC571`.
Bars are about 0.7 of their spacing.

### One trace

Columns over time truncate the years, as lines do, and tick only the labelled years.

```{r g24-bars-african-lion, econ_height = 165}
g24b_ethiopia <- data.frame(
  year = 2004:2015,
  growth = c(11.7, 12.7, 11.5, 11.8, 11.2, 10.0, 10.6, 11.4, 8.7, 9.8, 10.3, 8.7)
)

g24b_lion <- ggplot(g24b_ethiopia, aes(year, growth)) +
  geom_col(fill = single24[["print"]], width = 0.7) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 14), breaks = seq(0, 14, 2), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(seq(2004, 2014, 2), 2015), labels = c("2004", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "15*"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "African lion",
    subtitle = "Ethiopia’s GDP, % change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: IMF"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_lion, footnote = "*Estimate")
```

Against 2017: single-series red columns, a little wider, and no ticks under the unlabelled years. `r g24_2017("one-trace")`

### One trace with highlight

A highlighted category has its label set in bold.
Of the 11 print bar, column and stacked charts with a highlight, 8 mark it with a bold label alone (`20250524_STC394`, `20250524_STC444`, `20250104_IRC269`, `20240608_WBC178`, `20260829_FNC090`), and one also outlines its bar in black (`20250118_FBC388`).
Where the bars themselves must stand out, the rest go salmon and the highlight takes the deeper red, as the five bottom languages do in `20241005_EPC263`; this redraw follows that chart, since the 2017 version recolors the bar.

```{r g24-bars-salud, econ_height = 165}
g24b_doctors <- data.frame(
  country = c("Sweden", "Denmark", "Britain", "Portugal", "Luxembourg", "France", "Austria", "Spain", "Germany"),
  visits = c(2.9, 4.6, 5.0, 5.7, 6.3, 6.9, 6.9, 7.5, 8.2)
)
g24b_doctors$country <- factor(g24b_doctors$country, levels = g24b_doctors$country)
g24b_doctors$highlight <- g24b_doctors$country == "Spain"

g24b_salud <- ggplot(g24b_doctors, aes(country, visits, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 8.4), breaks = seq(0, 8, 2), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = g24_bold_label("Spain")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = p24[["salmon"]], `TRUE` = accent24[["print"]])) +
  labs(
    title = "Salud",
    subtitle = "Doctors’ consultations per person\nSelected countries, 2009",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: OECD"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_salud)
```

Against 2017: salmon bars with the highlight in red, where 2017 set a cyan bar among blue ones; the zero rule is black. `r g24_2017("one-trace-with-highlight")`

### Two traces

Two series take red and salmon, the first two colors of the palette, and are keyed above the plot with square swatches, the commonest key after direct labels (16 of 88 print charts).
The two bars of a pair touch, as in `20250104_IRC269`.

```{r g24-bars-defenders, econ_height = 235}
g24b_elections <- data.frame(
  country = rep(
    c("Chile", "Brazil", "Mexico", "Malaysia", "South Africa", "Poland", "India", "Egypt", "Russia"),
    each = 2
  ),
  income = rep(c("Middle class", "Low income"), 9),
  pct = c(80, 66, 69, 62, 64, 55, 61, 52, 59, 49, 54, 44, 53, 51, 51, 48, 51, 37)
)
g24b_elections$country <- factor(g24b_elections$country, levels = rev(unique(g24b_elections$country)))
g24b_elections$income <- factor(g24b_elections$income, levels = c("Middle class", "Low income"))

g24b_defenders <- ggplot(g24b_elections, aes(country, pct, fill = income)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 80), breaks = seq(0, 80, 20), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print") +
  labs(
    title = "Defenders of democracy",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Respondents saying that honest elections",
      "held regularly with a choice of at least two",
      "political parties are very important,",
      "2007, %",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Source: Pew Global Attitudes Survey"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_defenders)
```

Against 2017: red and salmon in place of two blues, and the pairs a little thicker. `r g24_2017("two-traces")`

### Two traces with sub-categories

The corpus has no bars grouped in two levels.
This redraw keeps the 2017 layout, each country a group named at its top left, and applies the general rules: red and salmon for the two forecasts, a key above the plot, the axis on top.

```{r g24-bars-autumn-fall, econ_height = 185}
g24b_forecasts <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("Germany", "France", "Euro area", "Spain", "Italy"), each = 4),
  vintage = rep(rep(c("2011", "2012"), each = 2), 5),
  made_in = rep(c("June", "September"), 10),
  gdp = c(3.2, 2.7, 2.0, 1.3, 2.1, 1.7, 1.9, 1.4, 2.0, 1.6, 1.7, 1.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1.6, 1.1, 1.0, 0.6, 1.3, 0.3)
)
g24b_forecasts$country <- factor(g24b_forecasts$country, levels = unique(g24b_forecasts$country))
g24b_forecasts$vintage <- factor(g24b_forecasts$vintage, levels = c("2012", "2011"))
g24b_forecasts$made_in <- factor(g24b_forecasts$made_in, levels = c("June", "September"))

## A rule above every group but the first.
g24b_autumn_rules <- data.frame(
  country = factor(levels(g24b_forecasts$country)[-1], levels = levels(g24b_forecasts$country))
)

g24b_autumn <- ggplot(g24b_forecasts, aes(vintage, gdp, fill = made_in)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(data = g24b_autumn_rules, aes(xintercept = 2.5), colour = econ$print$grid, linewidth = g24b_zero_lw) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(.data$country), scales = "free_y", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 3.3), breaks = 0:3, expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print") +
  labs(
    title = "Autumn fall",
    subtitle = "GDP, % increase on previous year",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Forecasts made in:", caption = "Source: IMF"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme() +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = g24_size, face = "plain", margin = margin(0, 4, 0, 0)
    ),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title.position = "top"))

g24_chart(g24b_autumn)
```

Against 2017: red and salmon for the two forecasts, in place of two blues. `r g24_2017("two-traces-with-sub-categories")`

Four series take the first four colors in order: red, salmon, blue, light blue.
The corpus has no grouped columns; this redraw keeps them touching, as grouped bars do.
Columns of categories rather than years have no ticks, as in `20260829_FNC090`.

```{r g24-bars-mighty-jungle, econ_height = 155}
g24b_returns <- data.frame(
  horizon = rep(c("20 years", "10 years", "5 years"), each = 4),
  asset = rep(c("Equities", "All property", "Rural property", "Forestry"), 3),
  pct = c(7.1, 8.7, 12.5, 9.5, 6.7, 6.1, 11.8, 18.8, 7.7, 10.9, 11.3, 21.1)
)
g24b_returns$horizon <- factor(g24b_returns$horizon, levels = c("20 years", "10 years", "5 years"))
g24b_returns$asset <- factor(
  g24b_returns$asset,
  levels = c("Equities", "All property", "Rural property", "Forestry")
)

g24b_jungle <- ggplot(g24b_returns, aes(horizon, pct, fill = asset)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.8) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 25), breaks = seq(0, 25, 5), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print") +
  labs(
    title = "The mighty jungle",
    subtitle = "Britain, annualised rate of return\non investment*, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "*To 2014\nSources: MSCI; JP Morgan"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme() +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

g24_chart(g24b_jungle)
```

Against 2017: red, salmon, blue and light blue in place of 2017's blues and cyans, standing on a black baseline, with the note above the source. `r g24_2017("two-traces-with-sub-categories")`

### One trace with a +/- axis

Negative values carry a plain minus sign and positive ones no sign; zero is a black rule, as in `20250524_STC394` and `20250104_IRC269`.
The bars keep one color on both sides of zero in both charts.
A summary row is set in bold, as "All" is in `20250104_IRC269`.

```{r g24-bars-dotcom, econ_height = 195}
g24b_capex <- data.frame(
  sector = c(
    "Internet", "Software", "Tech hardware", "IT services", "Health care", "Total", "Leisure", "Chemicals",
    "Oil, gas and fuels", "Metals and mining", "Property", "Energy equipment"
  ),
  change = c(52, 36, 26, 22, 9, -17, -19, -23, -32, -34, -35, -53)
)
g24b_capex$sector <- factor(g24b_capex$sector, levels = rev(g24b_capex$sector))

g24b_dotcom <- ggplot(g24b_capex, aes(sector, change)) +
  geom_col(fill = single24[["print"]], width = 0.7) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  ## Every 30, so the signed labels do not run together.
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-60, 60), breaks = seq(-60, 60, 30), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = g24_bold_label("Total")) +
  labs(
    title = "Another dotcom boom",
    subtitle = "Change in worldwide capital spending*, %\n2014-17 forecast",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "*In dollar terms\nSource: Goldman Sachs"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_dotcom)
```

Against 2017: single-series red bars from a black zero rule, where 2017 drew blue bars from a red one. `r g24_2017("one-trace-with-a---axis")`

> Differentiate positive/negative values by colour only where there is a
> meaningful difference i.e. imports / exports

The corpus has no chart that colors bars by sign.
Negative columns hang from the zero rule in the single-series red, as in `20250927_EUC526`, so this redraw draws inflows and outflows alike.

```{r g24-bars-money-drain, econ_height = 155}
## 2005 is missing from the 2017 guide's chart.
g24b_capital <- data.frame(
  year = c(1994:2004, 2006:2011),
  flow = c(-14, -4, -24, -18.5, -22, -21, -25, -15, -8, -1.5, -8, 42, 82, -134, -57, -34, -31.5)
)

g24b_drain <- ggplot(g24b_capital, aes(year, flow)) +
  geom_col(fill = single24[["print"]], width = 0.7) +
  g24b_zero() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-150, 100), breaks = seq(-150, 100, 50), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(seq(1994, 2008, 2), 2011),
    labels = c("1994", "96", "98", "2000", "02", "04", "06", "08", "11*"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1.5))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The money drain",
    subtitle = "Net private capital inflows/outflows, $bn",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: Central Bank of Russia"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_drain, footnote = "*To June 30th")
```

Against 2017: one red for inflows and outflows, where 2017 colored them apart, and a black zero rule. `r g24_2017("one-trace-with-a---axis")`

Where the sign does mean two things, as exports and imports do, the two are separate series and take red and salmon.
Panels are headed in bold under a short black rule, the lead-in bold and the rest regular, as "House 435 total seats" is in `20250118_FBC388`.
The series are named directly in the first panel, the commonest key in print (37 of 88 charts).

```{r g24-bars-trader-woes, econ_height = 215}
g24b_trade <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1995:2016, 4),
  country = rep(c("China, as % of GDP", "United States, as % of GDP"), each = 44),
  flow = rep(rep(c("Exports", "Imports"), each = 22), 2),
  pct = c(
    6.2, 5.9, 6.5, 6.9, 7.5, 8.2, 7.6, 8.5, 9.1, 10.0, 10.5,
    10.4, 9.0, 7.3, 5.8, 6.0, 5.3, 5.0, 4.7, 4.4, 4.3, 4.1,
    -1.5, -1.4, -1.2, -1.3, -1.2, -1.3, -1.4, -1.5, -1.7, -1.8, -1.7,
    -1.9, -1.8, -1.4, -1.4, -1.4, -1.3, -1.2, -1.2, -1.1, -0.95, -0.95,
    0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.15, 0.15, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35,
    0.4, 0.5, 0.55, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.7, 0.75, 0.75, 0.7, 0.7,
    -0.7, -0.75, -0.8, -0.9, -0.9, -1.1, -1.1, -1.2, -1.4,
    -1.6, -1.9, -2.1, -2.2, -2.3, -2.1, -2.5, -2.7, -2.7,
    -2.7, -2.75, -2.8, -2.6
  )
)
g24b_trade$country <- factor(g24b_trade$country, levels = c("China, as % of GDP", "United States, as % of GDP"))
g24b_trade$flow <- factor(g24b_trade$flow, levels = c("Exports", "Imports"))

## Only the China panel names its two series, beside their bars.
g24b_trade_labels <- data.frame(
  year = 1999.6,
  pct = c(9.9, -2.5),
  flow = factor(c("Exports", "Imports"), levels = levels(g24b_trade$flow)),
  country = factor(levels(g24b_trade$country)[1], levels = levels(g24b_trade$country))
)
g24b_trade_cols <- c(Exports = p24[["red"]], Imports = p24[["salmon"]])

g24b_woes <- ggplot(g24b_trade, aes(year, pct, fill = flow)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  g24b_zero() +
  geom_blank(
    data = data.frame(
      year = 1995,
      pct = c(-4, 12, -4, 4),
      country = factor(rep(levels(g24b_trade$country), each = 2), levels = levels(g24b_trade$country))
    ),
    aes(x = year, y = pct), inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = g24b_trade_labels, aes(x = year, y = pct, label = flow),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~country, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", axes = "all",
    labeller = as_labeller(
      c(
        `China, as % of GDP` = 'bold("China,")~"as % of GDP"',
        `United States, as % of GDP` = 'bold("United States,")~"as % of GDP"'
      ),
      label_parsed
    )
  ) +
  g24_value_axis(breaks = seq(-4, 12, 4), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24b_trade_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2016), labels = c("1995", "2000", "05", "10", "16*"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trader woes",
    subtitle = "China-United States trade in goods",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Census Bureau;\nIMF"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_woes, footnote = "*Jan-Nov annualised")
```

Against 2017: red and salmon for exports and imports, a black zero rule, and each panel heading under a short black rule. `r g24_2017("one-trace-with-a---axis")`

### Color overrides

> Where categories are chronological, use light-to-dark scale

The corpus has no grouped bars in time order.
The red ramp gives a light-to-dark scale in the palette's own hue: here its light step, salmon, and the deeper red.

```{r g24-bars-growth-asia, econ_height = 225}
g24b_asia <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("India", "Cambodia", "Laos", "China", "Malaysia", "Thailand", "Singapore", "Brunei"), each = 3),
  period = rep(c("2015", "2016", "2016-20*"), 8),
  growth = c(
    7.2, 7.3, 7.3, 7.0, 7.1, 7.3, 6.9, 7.0, 7.3, 6.8, 6.5, 6.0,
    4.6, 4.6, 5.0, 2.7, 3.1, 3.6, 2.1, 2.4, 2.6, -1.4, 0.5, 1.8
  )
)
g24b_asia$country <- factor(g24b_asia$country, levels = rev(unique(g24b_asia$country)))
g24b_asia$period <- factor(g24b_asia$period, levels = c("2015", "2016", "2016-20*"))

## Light to dark along the print red ramp.
g24b_chrono <- econ$print$sequential_red$value[c(2, 3, 5)]

g24b_growth <- ggplot(g24b_asia, aes(country, growth, fill = period)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-2, 8), breaks = seq(-2, 8, 2), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24b_chrono) +
  labs(
    title = "Growth in Asia",
    subtitle = "GDP forecasts, % change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "*Annual average\nSource: OECD"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_growth)
```

Against 2017: a red ramp in place of 2017's cyans and navy, and a black zero rule. `r g24_2017("color-overrides")`

> If categories form meaningful groups, use colour to reinforce that

Groups take a color family each, red and salmon for one, blue and light blue for the other, as the agreeing and disagreeing answers do in the web chart `20260117_WOC873`.

```{r g24-bars-dont-fence, econ_height = 235}
g24b_segregation <- data.frame(
  group = rep(
    c(
      "White British", "Other White", "Mixed", "Bangladeshi", "Pakistani", "Indian", "Chinese", "African",
      "Caribbean"
    ),
    each = 4
  ),
  area = rep(c("Inner London", "Outer London", "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities"), 9),
  change = c(
    3.0, 1.7, 1.6, 0.4, -2.7, -0.7, -1.7, 0, -6.3, -8.3, -10.4, -9.3,
    -0.1, -11.8, -3.7, -3.1, -1.0, -4.6, -3.0, -5.3, 0, -1.5, -5.3, -5.2,
    -6.1, -11.5, -11.9, -10.2, 0.3, -3.8, -14.8, -19.9, 1.3, -4.8, -4.7, -7.1
  )
)
g24b_segregation$group <- factor(g24b_segregation$group, levels = rev(unique(g24b_segregation$group)))
g24b_segregation$area <- factor(
  g24b_segregation$area,
  levels = c("Inner London", "Outer London", "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities")
)

g24b_fence <- ggplot(g24b_segregation, aes(group, change, fill = area)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-20, 5), breaks = seq(-20, 5, 5), expand = expansion(0)) +
  ## Reds for the two London rows, blues for the two city rows.
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(p24[c("red", "salmon", "blue", "light blue")])) +
  labs(
    title = "Don’t fence me in",
    subtitle = "Britain, % change in segregation index*\n2001-11",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "* % that needs to move to\ncreate an even distribution\nSource: University of Manchester"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme() +
  ## The key reads down its columns: London, then the cities.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE))

g24_chart(g24b_fence)
```

Against 2017: red and salmon for London and blue and light blue for the cities, where 2017 used its reds and blues; a black zero rule. `r g24_2017("color-overrides")`

## Bar / column, stacked

Stacked segments meet with no rule between them in print: `20240608_WBC178`, `20240803_EUC571`, `20240831_USC832`, `20260829_FNC090`.
Web stacks often outline each segment in a thin dark line (11 of the 18 stacked charts of 2026, such as `20260117_WOC873`; not `20260523_WOC503`).
The palette order usually runs from the baseline: red first, then salmon, blue, light blue and the grays, with "other" last in light gray, as in `20260829_FNC090`.
Of the 9 stacked print charts, 5 are keyed above the plot, 2 by direct labels, 1 by a key in the panel and 1 by a key at the left in stack order.
Segments wide enough carry their names or values inside them, white on red and blue and black on the lighter colors, as in `20240427_SRC663`.

```{r g24-bars-fed-nuptials, econ_height = 149}
g24b_carriers <- data.frame(
  band = rep(c("All mobiles", "Smartphones"), each = 5),
  carrier = rep(c("AT&T", "T-Mobile", "Sprint Nextel", "Verizon", "Other"), 2),
  share = c(30.4, 10.0, 31.4, 11.1, 16.8, 44.1, 9.6, 30.5, 12.9, 8.0),
  ## Segment widths as drawn in the 2017 guide.
  width = c(26.5, 10.1, 31.5, 11.0, 20.9, 35.1, 12.2, 29.6, 14.8, 8.3)
)
g24b_carriers$carrier <- factor(g24b_carriers$carrier, levels = unique(g24b_carriers$carrier))
g24b_carriers$band <- factor(g24b_carriers$band, levels = c("Smartphones", "All mobiles"))
g24b_carrier_fill <- setNames(unname(p24[c("red", "salmon", "blue", "light blue", "light gray")]), levels(g24b_carriers$carrier))
g24b_carriers$ink <- g24b_ink(g24b_carrier_fill[as.character(g24b_carriers$carrier)])
## Each bar is named above it, ranged left, in place of axis labels.
g24b_bands <- data.frame(band = levels(g24b_carriers$band), row = 1:2)

g24b_fed <- ggplot(g24b_carriers, aes(band, width, fill = carrier)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", share), colour = ink, group = carrier),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = g24_text
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = g24b_bands, aes(x = row + 0.31, y = 0, label = band), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.5))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24b_carrier_fill) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  labs(
    title = "The Fed says no to nuptials",
    subtitle = "Mobile operators' US market share\nJuly 2011, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Source: comScore"
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  g24_no_axes() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

g24_chart(g24b_fed)
```

Against 2017: the values centered in their segments, white on red and blue and black on the light colors, where 2017 set them all white at the segment's left edge; the key in stack order, "Other" last in light gray, not alphabetical. `r g24_2017("bar-column-stacked")`

Segments too small to name in place are named outside the bar on leader lines, each ending in a dot on its segment, as the proposed cuts are in `20250524_STC444`.
The one seat bar in the corpus, `20240706_WOC003`, marks the majority with a black rule through the bar, named beside it ("326 seats to win").
It draws British parties in their own colors; the corpus has no Spanish election, so the parties here take the palette.

```{r g24-bars-no-winner, econ_height = 129}
## Drawn in the 2017 guide's own units, so the leader lines can be placed.
g24b_seats <- data.frame(
  party = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Others", "Podemos", "PSOE", "Ciudadanos", "PP"),
  n = c(9, 8, 6, 5, 69, 90, 40, 123),
  ## The regional parties dark gray, others light gray, the four national parties in the palette's first four colors.
  fill = unname(p24[c("dark gray", "dark gray", "dark gray", "light gray", "salmon", "red", "light blue", "blue")])
)
g24b_seats$xmax <- cumsum(g24b_seats$n)
g24b_seats$xmin <- g24b_seats$xmax - g24b_seats$n
g24b_seats$mid <- (g24b_seats$xmin + g24b_seats$xmax) / 2
g24b_sx <- function(px) (px - 40) / 591 * 350
g24b_top <- 226
g24b_bottom <- 321

## The small parties and Ciudadanos are named beneath the bar, on leader lines that drop from their segments, turn
## right at staggered heights so as not to cross, and drop again to the names.
g24b_named <- data.frame(
  party = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Others", "Ciudadanos"),
  label_x = c(0, 47, 92, 180, 250),
  turn_y = c(392, 378, 363, 351, 351)
)
g24b_named$mid <- g24b_seats$mid[match(g24b_named$party, g24b_seats$party)]
g24b_named$label <- paste(g24b_named$party, g24b_seats$n[match(g24b_named$party, g24b_seats$party)])
g24b_paths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(g24b_named)), function(i) {
  d <- g24b_named[i, ]
  data.frame(party = d$party, x = c(d$mid, d$mid, d$label_x + 2, d$label_x + 2), y = c(g24b_bottom - 6, d$turn_y, d$turn_y, 394))
}))
g24b_dots <- data.frame(x = g24b_named$mid, y = g24b_bottom - 6)
g24b_names <- data.frame(x = g24b_named$label_x, y = 405, label = g24b_named$label)
## Values inside the big segments: the name, the seats beneath.
g24b_inside <- subset(g24b_seats, n >= 60)
g24b_inside$ink <- g24b_ink(g24b_inside$fill)

g24b_winner <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = g24b_seats, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = g24b_top, ymax = g24b_bottom, fill = fill),
    ## The three dark gray segments are told apart by a hairline of the ground.
    colour = econ$print$bg$value[1], linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_path(data = g24b_paths, aes(x, y, group = party), colour = econ$print$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = g24b_dots, aes(x, y), size = 0.6, colour = econ$print$text) +
  geom_text(data = g24b_names, aes(x, y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text) +
  geom_text(data = g24b_inside, aes(mid, 258, label = party, colour = ink), size = g24_text) +
  geom_text(data = g24b_inside, aes(mid, 292, label = n, colour = ink), size = g24_text) +
  ## The majority: a black rule through the bar, named above it.
  annotate("segment", x = 176, xend = 176, y = 205, yend = 340, colour = econ$print$text, linewidth = g24b_zero_lw * 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 176, y = 196, label = "176 required for majority", size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text,
           vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 350), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(425, 165), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "No one's a winner",
    subtitle = "Spanish general election 2015, Seats won",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Ministry of the Interior; El País"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24_no_axes()

g24_chart(g24b_winner)
```

Against 2017: the national parties in red, salmon, blue and light blue and the small parties in grays, where 2017 mixed its bar and stacked palettes; the majority is a black rule through the bar rather than a tick on a hand-drawn axis; leader lines end in dots on their segments. `r g24_2017("bar-column-stacked")`

The corpus has no stacked bars drawn to different scales in one chart.
This redraw keeps the 2017 layout and applies the panel rules: each bar is headed under a short black rule, the lead-in bold, as each panel is in `20250118_FBC388`.
A breakdown with more than four parts uses the six colors in order.

```{r g24-bars-looting, econ_height = 189}
## Drawn in the 2017 guide's own units; each bar has its own scale.
g24b_bars <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    row = 1, stream = c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity"),
    value = c(20.1, 14.3, 12.0, 4.0), scale = 617 / 50.4, x0 = 33, fill = unname(p24[1:4])
  ),
  data.frame(
    row = 2, stream = c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity"),
    value = c(2.3, 3.8, 1.9, 0.4), scale = 61.2, x0 = 37, fill = unname(p24[1:4])
  ),
  data.frame(
    row = 3, stream = c("Fighters' salary", "Military camps", "Social services", "Islamic police", "Treasury", "Media"),
    value = c(2.5, 1.15, 1.0, 0.6, 0.35, 0.2), scale = 61.2, x0 = 37, fill = unname(p24[1:6])
  )
)
g24b_bars$xmax <- unlist(lapply(split(g24b_bars, g24b_bars$row), function(d) d$x0 + cumsum(d$value) * d$scale))
g24b_bars$xmin <- g24b_bars$xmax - g24b_bars$value * g24b_bars$scale
g24b_bars$ymin <- c(258, 452, 592)[g24b_bars$row]
g24b_bars$ymax <- c(312, 497, 632)[g24b_bars$row]
g24b_bars$mid <- (g24b_bars$xmin + g24b_bars$xmax) / 2
g24b_first <- subset(g24b_bars, row == 1)
g24b_first$label <- c("20.1", "14.3", "12.0", "4")
g24b_first$ink <- g24b_ink(g24b_first$fill)

## Panel headings: a bold lead-in, then the rest, under a short black rule as long as the tab.
g24b_headings <- data.frame(
  y = c(188, 380, 548),
  label = c(
    'bold("Overall")~"Monthly revenue $79.8m"',
    'bold("Deir al-Zor governorate")~"Monthly revenue $8.7m"',
    'bold("Monthly spending")~"$5.8m"'
  )
)
g24b_rules <- data.frame(y = c(163, 353, 523))
## The first bar's key runs along its heading; the third bar's names have leader lines.
g24b_keys <- data.frame(
  x = c(38, 221, 428, 521, 40, 170, 640, 640, 640, 640),
  y = c(237, 237, 237, 237, 655, 655, 571, 610, 646, 686),
  label = c(
    "Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity", "Fighters'\nsalary", "Military\ncamps",
    "Treasury", "Media", "Islamic police", "Social services"
  ),
  fill = c(unname(p24[1:4]), g24b_bars$fill[g24b_bars$row == 3][c(1, 2, 5, 6, 4, 3)])
)
g24b_keys$left <- g24b_keys$x < 600
## Leader lines from the segments to the names on the right, as (x, y) corners.
g24b_lead <- list(
  Treasury = list(x = c(369, 369, 495), y = c(600, 571, 571)),
  Media = list(x = c(386, 386, 525), y = c(612, 610, 610)),
  Police = list(x = c(340, 340, 435), y = c(625, 646, 646)),
  Social = list(x = c(291, 291, 415), y = c(625, 686, 686))
)
g24b_lead_paths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(g24b_lead), function(nm) {
  data.frame(id = nm, x = g24b_lead[[nm]]$x, y = g24b_lead[[nm]]$y)
}))
## The middle bar's own 0--10 axis: labels above, rules through the bar.
g24b_ticks <- data.frame(x = 37 + 61.2 * seq(0, 10, 2), label = seq(0, 10, 2))
g24b_ticks$colour <- ifelse(g24b_ticks$x == 37, econ$print$text, econ$print$grid)

g24b_looting <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = g24b_ticks, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 437, yend = 510, colour = colour), linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(data = g24b_ticks, aes(x, 422, label = label), size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text) +
  geom_rect(data = g24b_bars, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(data = g24b_first, aes(mid, 285, label = label, colour = ink), size = g24_text) +
  geom_segment(
    data = g24b_rules, aes(x = 33, xend = 33 + 100, y = y, yend = y), colour = econ$print$text, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    ## At the axis-label size, so the longest heading fits the width.
    data = g24b_headings, aes(33, y, label = label), parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = g24_text,
    colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  geom_path(data = g24b_lead_paths, aes(x, y, group = id), colour = econ$print$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(
    data = data.frame(x = c(369, 386, 340, 291), y = c(600, 612, 625, 625)), aes(x, y), size = 0.6,
    colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  geom_rect(data = g24b_keys, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 10, ymin = y - 10, ymax = y + 10, fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(g24b_keys, left), aes(x + 16, y + ifelse(y > 600, 16, 0), label = label), hjust = 0,
    lineheight = 1.1, size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(g24b_keys, !left), aes(x - 9, y, label = label), hjust = 1, size = g24_text,
    colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(32, 652), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(715, 150), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Looting the Levant",
    subtitle = "Islamic State's finances*, January 2015, $m",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "*Estimates\nSource: IHS"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24_no_axes()

g24_chart(g24b_looting)
```

Against 2017: the six colors in order for both breakdowns, where 2017 gave the spending bar its own set; black rules over all three headings, where 2017 drew red ones over two. `r g24_2017("bar-column-stacked")`

A forecast is a band of darker gray the full height of the panel, named at its top in gray, as in `20260829_FNC025`.
The key sits above the plot, the commonest place for a stacked chart's key.

```{r g24-bars-getting-sociable, econ_height = 178}
g24b_adspend <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2008:2017, each = 4),
  format = rep(c("Paid search", "Display", "Classified", "Online video"), 10),
  bn = c(
    24, 15, 9, 4, 27, 16, 9, 4, 32, 19, 9, 6, 37, 19, 10, 10,
    43, 21, 11, 15, 48, 25, 11, 20, 56, 27, 13, 27, 62, 31, 15, 36,
    72, 33, 16, 44, 79, 35, 17, 54
  )
)
g24b_adspend$format <- factor(g24b_adspend$format, levels = unique(g24b_adspend$format))

g24b_sociable <- ggplot(g24b_adspend, aes(year, bn, fill = format)) +
  ## The forecast years: a darker band, named at its top.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2014.5, xmax = 2017.5, ymin = 0, ymax = 228, fill = econ$print$sequential_gray$value[2]) +
  annotate("text", x = 2016, y = 222, label = "Forecast", size = g24_text, colour = econ$print$source, vjust = 1) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 228), breaks = seq(0, 200, 50), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2017), labels = c("2008", "10", "12", "14", "16", "17"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1.4))
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print") +
  labs(
    title = "Getting sociable",
    subtitle = "Global internet-advertising spending, $bn",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Source: ZenithOptimedia"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

g24_chart(g24b_sociable)
```

Against 2017: red, salmon, blue and light blue in place of 2017's blue, cyan, gold and teal; the key above the plot rather than inside it, and the forecast named in gray sentence case under no rule. `r g24_2017("bar-column-stacked")`

A stack below zero hangs from the black zero rule, as the deficits do in `20260829_FNC025`.

```{r g24-bars-more-in-out, econ_height = 179}
## China's share, and the total.
g24b_china <- c(
  0.15, 0.18, 0.26, 0.29, 0.37, 0.40, 0.46, 0.55, 0.61, 0.68, 0.79, 0.75, 0.92, 1.05,
  1.30, 1.52, 1.67, 1.76, 1.80, 1.54, 1.80, 1.87, 1.93, 1.89, 1.96, 2.02, 1.83
)
g24b_total <- c(
  1.67, 1.05, 1.27, 1.65, 2.04, 2.06, 2.07, 2.07, 2.50, 3.38, 4.22, 3.85, 4.24, 4.61,
  5.32, 5.89, 5.96, 5.58, 5.52, 3.47, 4.22, 4.66, 4.50, 4.11, 4.20, 4.11, 3.87
)
g24b_deficit <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1990:2016, 2),
  region = rep(c("China", "Rest of world"), each = 27),
  pct = c(-g24b_china, -(g24b_total - g24b_china))
)
g24b_deficit$region <- factor(g24b_deficit$region, levels = c("China", "Rest of world"))

g24b_more_in <- ggplot(g24b_deficit, aes(year, pct, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  g24b_zero() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-6, 0), breaks = -6:0, expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2016), labels = c("1990", "95", "2000", "05", "10", "16*"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 2))
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print") +
  labs(
    title = "More in than out",
    subtitle = "United States, merchandise-trade deficit\n% of GDP",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Sources: US Census Bureau;\nUS Bureau of Economic\nAnalysis"
  ) +
  g24b_cols_theme()

g24_chart(g24b_more_in, footnote = "*January-September")
```

Against 2017: red and salmon in place of blue and cyan, a black zero rule, and ticks under the labelled years only. `r g24_2017("bar-column-stacked")`

### Color overrides

> You may need to swap in other colours for charts with more than 4 categories
>
> Use grey for ‘other’ / ‘dont know’ etc

The six colors take six categories; "other" is light gray and comes last, as in `20260829_FNC090`.
Beyond six, the web charts add tints: a pale red after salmon and steps of gray, as in `20260516_WOC990`.
This chart has six origins and "other", so it takes the pale red step of the red ramp after salmon.
As in the 100% stack `20240427_SRC663`, no gridlines show between the bars.

```{r g24-bars-movers-shakers, econ_height = 179}
## Origins in stack order; a bar skips origins it lacks.
g24b_origins <- c("Romania", "Poland", "Italy", "Portugal", "Germany", "Britain")
g24b_shares <- rbind(
  `EU-28` = c(20, 15, 9, 7.5, 5, 0),
  Switzerland = c(0, 0, 20.5, 21, 24, 0),
  Germany = c(5.5, 17.5, 18.5, 0, 0, 0),
  Spain = c(46.5, 0, 9.5, 6, 0, 8),
  France = c(0, 0, 7.5, 42, 0, 8),
  Italy = c(76, 7.5, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  Britain = c(5.5, 29.5, 0, 5.5, 0, 0)
)
g24b_migrants <- data.frame(
  destination = rep(rownames(g24b_shares), times = ncol(g24b_shares) + 1),
  origin = rep(c(g24b_origins, "Other"), each = nrow(g24b_shares)),
  pct = c(g24b_shares, 100 - rowSums(g24b_shares))
)
g24b_migrants$origin <- factor(g24b_migrants$origin, levels = c(g24b_origins, "Other"))
g24b_migrants$destination <- factor(g24b_migrants$destination, levels = rev(rownames(g24b_shares)))

## Red, salmon, then the ramp's pale red; blue, light blue and dark gray; light gray for "other".
g24b_movers_cols <- c(
  p24[["red"]], p24[["salmon"]], econ$print$sequential_red$value[2], p24[["blue"]], p24[["light blue"]],
  p24[["dark gray"]], p24[["light gray"]]
)

g24b_movers <- ggplot(g24b_migrants, aes(destination, pct, fill = origin)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  g24b_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = g24_bold_label("EU-28")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(g24b_movers_cols, c(g24b_origins, "Other"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Movers and shakers",
    subtitle = "Intra-European* migrants living elsewhere\n2014, % of total by destination country",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "*Including EFTA\nSource: European Commission"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

g24_chart(g24b_movers)
```

Against 2017: the 2024 six colors and a pale red, with "Other" in the key, last, in light gray, where 2017 named it in the panel. `r g24_2017("color-overrides-1")`

> If categories form meaningful groups, use colour to reinforce that

Answers on a scale take a family for each side and gray for the middle: blue and light blue for the content, salmon and red for the discontent, light gray for "not sure", as in `20260117_WOC873`.
A second measure for each bar goes in a column of gray circles sized by value, headed by a label in a gray box that points down at them, as in `20250531_WBC482`.

```{r g24-bars-trumps-troops, econ_height = 249}
g24b_answers <- c("Enthusiastic", "Satisfied", "Dissatisfied", "Upset", "Not sure")
## Rows top to bottom.
g24b_troops <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "White men\nno college", "White women\nno college", "White men\ncollege educated",
    "Non-white men\ncollege educated", "White women\ncollege educated", "Non-white men\nno college",
    "Non-white women\ncollege educated", "Non-white women\nno college"
  ),
  share = c(22, 24, 16, 3, 17, 6, 4, 7)
)
g24b_troops$row <- rev(seq_len(nrow(g24b_troops)))
g24b_pct <- rbind(
  c(29, 24, 14, 31, 2), c(25, 19, 13, 40, 3), c(18, 17, 17, 47, 1), c(18, 12, 11, 51, 8),
  c(13, 15, 14, 57, 1), c(11, 12, 19, 52, 6), c(4, 9, 15, 70, 2), c(5, 7, 17, 67, 4)
)
g24b_feel <- data.frame(
  row = rep(g24b_troops$row, times = length(g24b_answers)),
  answer = factor(rep(g24b_answers, each = nrow(g24b_troops)), levels = g24b_answers),
  pct = c(g24b_pct)
)
g24b_left <- -83

g24b_trump <- ggplot(g24b_feel, aes(row, pct, fill = answer)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  g24b_zero() +
  ## Each row is named in two lines, ranged left.
  geom_text(
    data = g24b_troops, aes(row, g24b_left, label = name), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, lineheight = 0.8,
    size = g24_pt(6.3), colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  ## The second measure: gray circles sized by value, right of the 100% mark.
  geom_point(data = g24b_troops, aes(row, 120, size = share), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = p24[["light gray"]]) +
  geom_text(
    data = g24b_troops, aes(row, 120, label = share), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = g24_text,
    colour = econ$print$text
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label_economist_2017", x = 9.6, y = 120, label = "% of total voters\n2012", pointer = "bottom",
    hjust = 0.82, padding = 2, fill = p24[["light gray"]], colour = econ$print$text, size = g24_text,
    family = economist_2017_font()
  ) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.55, 8.45), clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6.5, guide = "none") +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(g24b_left, 134), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = unname(c(p24[c("blue", "light blue", "salmon", "red", "light gray")]))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trump's troops",
    subtitle = "How do you feel about Donald Trump as\nthe 2016 Republican nominee\nfor president?*",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "*5,773 registered voters surveyed\nJune 4th to July 9th 2016\nSources: YouGov; CCES; The Economist"
  ) +
  g24b_bars_theme() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = FALSE))

g24_chart(g24b_trump)
```

Against 2017: blue and light blue for the content and salmon and red for the discontent, where 2017 mixed its stacked and bar palettes; light gray circles with black figures for the second measure, where 2017 drew blue-gray circles with white ones; the row names in one weight. `r g24_2017("color-overrides-1")`
